iut_type: End Product (Nippon Seimitsu Sokki blood pressure monitor), free derivative registration for a different device type and forward-looking Design Name strategy
customer_question: If we later want to register a completely different product type (a pulse oximeter, instead of our initial blood pressure monitor), using the same module and same QDID references, can it be added to our initial registration for free?
question_variants: Does the derivative-registration-is-free rule depend on the product type being similar, or just on the module/QDID being the same?
What Design Name should be used if more product types are expected to be added later?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to know whether a free derivative addition to their registration was available not just for variants of the same product (e.g., different blood pressure monitor models) but for an entirely different device category (a pulse oximeter), as long as the same module and QDID references were used, and how to best set up the registration to accommodate this future addition.
plain_english_explanation: Free derivative registration to the Product List is available for any subsequent product that implements the same module and the same Host Stack as the initially-registered product -- the rule is tied to the underlying Bluetooth implementation being identical, not to the product category or device type being similar. This meant the customer's planned future pulse oximeter, despite being a functionally different device category from the initial blood pressure monitor, could still be added for free as long as it used the same module/QDID references. Because of this, the consultant recommended that the registration's Design Name (the name that's locked in from the first Product List entry, separate from the more flexible per-entry Product Name) be chosen as a broader, category-spanning term like 'Health Device' rather than narrowly tied to the initial product (which would otherwise default to something like 'Blood pressure monitor'), specifically to better accommodate the different device types the customer already anticipated adding later.
consultant_answer: Yes -- free derivative registration depends on using the same module and the same Host Stack, not on the product category being similar, so your planned pulse oximeter can be added for free even though it's a different device type from your blood pressure monitor. Given that you already anticipate adding different device types, we'd recommend using a broader, category-spanning Design Name like 'Health Device' rather than something narrowly tied to the blood pressure monitor, since the Design Name gets locked in from your first Product List entry.
decision_logic: Free derivative registration eligibility is determined by whether a subsequent product implements the same module and Host Stack as the initially-registered product, regardless of whether the product category or device type differs -- when a customer signals they expect to register multiple different device types under the same underlying Bluetooth implementation, recommend a Design Name broad enough to span all anticipated types, since it's locked in from the first registration entry.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks about adding a different device type as a free derivative, clarify that the determining factor is the shared module/Host Stack, not product similarity -- and proactively recommend a forward-looking, category-spanning Design Name if the customer signals plans for future device types under the same Bluetooth implementation.
risk_if_done_wrong: Locking in a narrowly-scoped Design Name (e.g., tied specifically to 'blood pressure monitor') without anticipating future different device types could create naming confusion or an awkward-looking registration once an unrelated device category is added as a derivative later.
